text: A long, close-fitting man's overcoat. The 'frogs' are the ornamental braid fastenings across the front, a military look that was decades out of date in 1838 Paris.
quote: dressed in one of the green surtouts

text: A small city-state in Tuscany, in 1838 still an independent duchy. Its old families claimed proud descent, which makes it a handy birthplace for an invented nobleman.
quote: a worthy patrician of Lucca

text: After 1815 Austria ruled Lombardy and Venetia and dominated the rest of Italy, so many Italians served in its army. The French rather looked down on Austrian officers, as the count jokes.
quote: Ex-major in the Austrian service?

text: A sweet, dark Spanish dessert wine from the region of Alicante, often taken with a biscuit.
quote: Alicante, if you please; it is my favorite wine.

text: Italian: 'By Bacchus!' (a mild oath) and 'Oh, what a pity!'
quote: Ah, _perbacco_, indispensable, were they?

term: Marriage is a civil affair in France
text: Since the Revolution a French marriage has been legally valid only when performed by a civil official (the mayor), backed by birth and identity papers. A church wedding alone counted for nothing in law.
quote: Marriage is a civil affair in France

text: A fortune for a shabby old soldier. A Paris labourer earned perhaps 1.5–2 francs a day, so this is decades of wages; very roughly, a franc then bought what €10–20 buys now.
quote: credit on you for the further sum of 48,000 francs

text: Medals and badges of chivalric orders, worn on the coat on formal occasions. France had mocked such decorations since the Revolution yet still prized them, as the count says.
quote: Do not forget your crosses.

text: Italian cities kept a 'golden book' (libro d'oro) listing their noble families. To be 'inscribed in the golden book' was proof of ancient nobility.
quote: inscribed in the golden book at Florence

text: A town on the frontier between France and Savoy, which then belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia. Crossing there meant entering France from Italy.
quote: from Pont-de-Beauvoisin to Paris

text: In the ancient Roman world educated Greek slaves, many from Asia Minor (modern Turkey), were prized as tutors, doctors and secretaries, and fetched high prices.
quote: the slaves were treated in Asia Minor

text: A proverb from Thomas à Kempis's devotional classic The Imitation of Christ (15th century): we make plans, but their outcome is not in our hands.
quote: man proposes, and God disposes

text: The dialect of Florence, the basis of literary Italian. Speaking 'very excellent Tuscan' marks Andrea as well schooled, and lets the two men talk privately in French company.
quote: he said, in very excellent Tuscan

text: A light, fast, open four-wheeled carriage with large wheels, driven by its owner: the sports car of a fashionable young man.
quote: if you purchase a phaeton

text: Full evening dress for a formal dinner: an officer wore uniform and decorations; civilians of the old school still wore knee-breeches rather than trousers.
quote: uniform, cross, knee-breeches

text: Lucerne is alfalfa, a clover-like fodder crop. The chapter title refers to the field of it outside the Villefort garden, where Maximilian waits by the gate.
A woman who became a nun renounced the world and her property. Valentine's fortune would then have passed to her father and, after him, to her half-brother.
quote: Now, if I had taken the veil

text: A legal term: property that passes to someone after another person's interest in it ends. Here the money would go first to Villefort, then on to Edward.
quote: and, in reversion, to his son

term: sabring right and left among the Bedouins
text: France had been conquering Algeria since 1830, and cavalry like Maximilian's Spahis fought the Arab and Berber tribes there. Médéah, the name he gives his horse, is an Algerian town taken by the French.
quote: sabring right and left among the Bedouins

text: The price of the horse: around eight years' pay for a labourer, and a serious sum even for an army captain living on modest means.
quote: they told me it was 4,500 francs

text: A light two-wheeled, one-horse carriage with a folding hood: the Paris cab of the day (and the origin of the word 'cab').
quote: so I took a cabriolet

text: A mirror. Placed opposite Noirtier, it lets him see the whole room without being able to turn his head.
quote: He was placed before a large glass

text: Noirtier's state, mind intact but body frozen except for the eyes, is what doctors now call locked-in syndrome, usually caused by a stroke in the brainstem.
quote: took their places on either side of the paralytic

text: French: boredom, weariness. Villefort could talk with his father through the eye signals but rarely bothers to.
quote: indifference and _ennui_ which prevented him

text: The notary is describing a sealed (or 'mystic') will under French law: the testator approves the document before seven witnesses, and the notary seals it in their presence.
quote: provided it be read in the presence of seven witnesses

text: A great fortune. Invested in government stock (rentes) at about 4–5 per cent, it would bring roughly 40,000 a year: perhaps a hundred times a working family's income.
quote: You are then in possession of 900,000 francs?

text: The two classic forms of wealth: land, which earned rents, or government bonds and shares. Noirtier keeps his as bank scrip, paper certificates locked in a casket.
quote: found 900,000 francs in bank scrip

text: The person who inherits whatever remains of an estate after specific gifts and debts are paid: in effect, the main heir.
quote: your residuary legatee?

term: the law does not allow a son to be entirely deprived
text: The Napoleonic Code reserves a fixed share of every estate for the children (the réserve). A parent may freely leave only the rest, so a will giving everything away can be challenged in court.
quote: the law does not allow a son to be entirely deprived

text: The radical left of the revolutionary National Convention (1792–95), so called because its members sat on the highest benches. It led the Terror, and was willing to use any means.
quote: the terrible theories of The Mountain

term: the senator's robe, which Napoleon cast on his shoulders
text: Napoleon gave many former revolutionaries seats in his Senate, a richly paid and largely ceremonial body. Villefort means the honour bought his father's dignity, not his loyalty.
quote: the senator’s robe, which Napoleon cast on his shoulders

text: Brother of Louis XVIII and King of France from 1824 until the July Revolution of 1830 drove him out. He made many royalist creations of nobility.
quote: created Baron d’Épinay by Charles X.

text: Not the electric telegraph but the Chappe optical system: towers on hilltops, each with jointed black wooden arms whose positions were read by telescope and repeated down the line. A message could cross France in hours.
quote: its black arms, bending in every direction

text: Real politicians who served as Minister of the Interior under Louis-Philippe. The telegraph belonged to the government, and only that ministry could send messages on it.
quote: a sign from M. Duchâtel, or from M. Montalivet

text: Greek: 'far' and 'to write'. Together they make 'telegraph', far-writing.
quote: two Greek words, _têle_, _graphein_

term: half a league from the Barriers
text: A league was about 4 km (2.5 miles). The Barriers were the gates in the customs wall around Paris, where duty was charged on goods entering the city.
quote: only half a league from the Barriers

text: One of the gates in the customs wall on the south side of Paris, leading to the Orléans road. Its name means 'Gate of Hell'; the square there is today's Place Denfert-Rochereau.
quote: the Barrière d’Enfer, taking the road to

text: The keep of a ruined medieval castle on a hill about 25 km south of Paris. A real telegraph station was set up on it, on the Paris–Bayonne line toward Spain.
quote: reached the tower of Montlhéry

text: The Romans fattened dormice in jars and ate them as a delicacy, preserved in honey. Petronius describes them at a banquet in his comic novel the Satyricon.
quote: I have read so in Petronius

term: A thousand francs … A hundred crowns
text: The operator's pay is under 3 francs a day, with lodging; his future pension is 300 francs a year (a crown, or écu, here meaning 3 francs). The 25,000 the count offers is twenty-five years' salary.
quote: And how much is the pension?

term: Don Carlos has fled from Bourges
text: Don Carlos, pretender to the Spanish throne, had lost the Carlist civil war in 1839 and was interned by the French government at Bourges. His escape would mean renewed war, and Spanish government bonds would plunge.
quote: Because Don Carlos has fled from Bourges

text: Le Messager was an evening paper close to the government that printed telegraph news; Le Moniteur was the government's official gazette. A denial in the Moniteur was final.
quote: Next morning _Le Moniteur_ contained the following

term: The funds rose one per cent
text: 'The funds' are government bonds. Prices moved by fractions of a per cent, so a one per cent swing on millions of francs meant a fortune made or lost overnight.
quote: The funds rose one per cent higher

text: A courtier of Louis XIV famed for flattery: he had a whole avenue of trees felled overnight because it spoiled the king's view.
quote: the Duc d’Antin removed in a single night

text: Old masters: Dutch landscape and genre painters (Hobbema, Paulus Potter, Mieris, Gerard Dou), alongside Raphael, Van Dyck and the Spaniards Zurbarán and Murillo. Owning all of these was princely.
quote: here are two by Hobbema, a Paul Potter

text: The Louvre, the national picture gallery. Debray's point is that the government could not afford the painting the count simply bought.
quote: it was proposed for the Museum

text: A stiff, wide neckband, fastened behind, worn instead of a cravat, especially by military men.
quote: A black satin stock, fresh from the maker’s hands

text: French: pregnant. Polite English of the period often borrowed the French word.
quote: she that was _enceinte_

term: Macbeth uses to point out Banquo
text: In Shakespeare's Macbeth the murdered Banquo's ghost appears at a feast, and Macbeth points at it in terror while his guests see nothing.
quote: the gesture Macbeth uses to point out Banquo

text: A 'cover' is a place setting at table; Bertuccio is asking how many guests to lay for.
quote: How many covers?

text: A famously extravagant Roman gourmet whose name was attached to the only surviving ancient cookbook.
quote: like one of the displays with which Apicius

text: A louis was a 20-franc gold coin, so this is 20,000 francs for one dinner for ten: several lifetimes of the telegraph man's pay.
quote: possible to expend a thousand louis upon a dinner

term: eating pearls, like Cleopatra … drinking refined gold
text: Cleopatra is said to have dissolved a priceless pearl in vinegar and drunk it to win a bet with Mark Antony; Lorenzo de' Medici was reputed to take dissolved gold as medicine.
quote: eating pearls, like Cleopatra

text: The sterlet is a small sturgeon of Russia's Volga, highly prized; the lamprey is an eel-like fish, here from Lake Fusaro near Naples. Moving them alive across Europe in 1838 was absurdly difficult.
quote: This one is, I think, a sterlet

text: Latin: 'a lover of the impossible'. The Roman historian Tacitus applied the phrase to Nero.
quote: I am like Nero—_cupitor impossibilium_

text: A celebrated beauty murdered in 1667 by her brothers-in-law, the Abbé and the Chevalier de Ganges: a notorious true-crime story Dumas himself retold.
quote: the chamber of the Marquise de Ganges

term: Ugolino's tower … Tasso's prison … Francesca and Paolo
text: Famous Italian sites of suffering: the tower in Pisa where Count Ugolino starved (Dante's Inferno), the cell in Ferrara where the poet Tasso was confined, and the Rimini room of Dante's doomed lovers.
quote: we have at Pisa, Ugolino’s tower

text: The Roman goddess of childbirth.
quote: a bed visited by the goddess Lucina

text: Under the Napoleonic Penal Code, killing a newborn child was punished by death, by guillotine.
quote: What is done to infanticides in this country?

text: A light, open, two-wheeled carriage for one horse, driven by its owner with a groom perched behind: very much the young dandy's vehicle.
quote: Andrea Cavalcanti found his tilbury

text: A large four-wheeled carriage with a hood at each end that can be folded back, used for family outings.
quote: He offered a seat in his landau

text: Latin: 'to be astonished at nothing'. Horace's advice for a calm, happy life; also the pose of a true man of the world.
quote: faithful to the principle of Horace, _nil admirari_

text: Italian: a porter, or a tourist guide.
quote: by acting as _facchino_ or _cicerone_

text: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet, the great 17th-century bishop and preacher. Caderousse means 'thank you for the sermon'.
quote: Do you think so, M. Bossuet?

text: After the 1830 revolution, seats in the Chamber of Peers stopped being hereditary (1831): a peer of France could no longer pass the title to his son.
quote: but then, hereditary rank is abolished

text: Convicts in the prison hulks and labour camps (bagnes) of Toulon were known by number, not name. An escapee caught without papers would simply be sent back.
quote: Then I should become simply No. 106

term: Place Louis XV. … Pont de la Révolution
text: Old names for today's Place de la Concorde and Pont de la Concorde. The square changed name with each regime; Parisians often kept using the earlier one.
quote: At the Place Louis XV. the three young people separated

text: Latin: 'of her own accord', without being asked.
quote: receive an avowal _proprio motu_

text: A river in ancient Lydia whose sands carried gold, said to be where King Midas washed off his golden touch. Demoustier was an 18th-century writer of popular mythology.
quote: My money boxes are my Pactolus

text: In 1825 France forced Haiti to pay a huge indemnity, 150 million francs, for recognizing its independence. Haiti borrowed in Paris and often missed payments, so Haitian bonds were a gamble.
quote: you were the first who told me of the Haitian funds

text: His supporters called Don Carlos 'Charles V' of Spain. The Bidassoa is the river on the French–Spanish border; crossing it meant leaving Spain, defeated, in 1839.
quote: the day Charles V. repassed the Bidassoa

text: An allowance given to a wife for her personal spending, such as clothes. Danglars's 250,000 francs is a satirical 'allowance'.
quote: 250,000 francs were paid to you for pin-money

text: The Paris opera house devoted to Italian opera, the most fashionable in the city, whose star singers were the celebrities of the day.
quote: made such a successful appearance at the Théâtre Italien

term: inscribed his name to speak against the budget
text: Danglars is a deputy in the Chamber, where members signed up in advance to speak. As an opposition member he attacks the government's budget.
quote: inscribed his name to speak against the budget

text: A merchant who 'suspends payment' stops honouring his debts: in effect, bankruptcy. Bills of exchange (written orders to pay) drawn on him come back unpaid.
quote: my fine Jacopo Manfredi suspends payment

text: 'Animal magnetism', or mesmerism, was a fashionable belief that an invisible fluid linked people and could produce trances and prophetic dreams.
quote: It is magnetism, she says

term: the seven fat and the seven lean kine
text: In Genesis, Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones; Joseph interprets it as seven years of plenty followed by seven of famine.
quote: Recollect the seven fat and the seven lean kine

text: Literally 'beyond the mountains': from across the Alps, that is, Italian.
quote: these ultramontane millionaires

text: Italian: chief magistrates of medieval Italian cities, and the mercenary captains who fought their wars.
quote: all these old _podestàs_, these ancient _condottieri_

text: El Dorado was the legendary South American city of gold; Potosí, in Bolivia, was a real mountain of silver that enriched Spain for centuries.
quote: an El Dorado, and Potosí

term: Dieppe for the benefit of sea air
text: Dieppe, on the Normandy coast, was a fashionable sea-bathing resort; doctors prescribed sea air for many complaints.
quote: obliged to go to Dieppe for the benefit of sea air

text: French: upstarts, people newly risen to wealth or rank without the background society expects.
quote: being both parvenus, both having become noble

term: the Palais … the Salle des Pas-Perdus
text: The Palais de Justice, the law courts on the Île de la Cité, entered from the Rue de Harlay. The Salle des Pas-Perdus ('hall of lost footsteps') is its vast waiting hall, always crowded with lawyers and clients.
quote: Madame Danglars soon reached the Salle des Pas-Perdus

text: A legal deed cancelling a lease before its term ends.
quote: made the tenant sign the deed of resilition

term: Four men carried me from Paris to Châlons
text: Before railways, an invalid too weak for a jolting coach might be carried in a litter, then sent by river boat down the Saône and Rhône toward the south.
quote: Four men carried me from Paris to Châlons

text: A lantern with a sliding shutter, so its light can be hidden or directed in a narrow beam.
quote: I had provided myself with a dark lantern

text: Paris's Hospice des Enfants-Trouvés took in abandoned babies. Parents often left a token, such as half a torn card or cloth, so they could later prove their claim and take the child back.
quote: he had put it in the foundling hospital

text: Noble families marked their linen with the coronet of their rank and an initial. The baron's coronet points to her first husband's title.
quote: marked with half a baron’s crown, and the letter H

text: Fairy queens from Shakespeare: Queen Mab from Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet, Titania from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
quote: if I had taken Queen Mab or Titania as my companion

text: Fashionable Paris jewellers of the day; Fossin was among the most famous, supplying the royal family.
quote: glittered in the window at Marlé’s or Fossin’s

text: The count plays on Albert's 'electric shock' of sympathy: the electric telegraph wire was the newest marvel of science.
quote: the magnetic wire I was guiding acted

text: High society usually left Paris for country estates after the spring season. 'Those who remain in Paris in July' are the truly devoted Parisians, so a July ball is select.
quote: Summer balls are fashionable.

text: An 18th-century adventurer at the court of Louis XV who hinted that he was centuries old and owned an elixir of life.
quote: Cagliostro or the Count Saint-Germain

text: Henri-François d'Aguesseau (1668–1751), Chancellor of France, a byword for stern legal integrity. Albert applies the name to Villefort.
quote: We shall try to persuade the great d’Aguesseau

text: The head of the Paris police, a powerful government appointee. Boville has risen from inspector of prisons to a senior post under him.
quote: from the prefect of police?

text: French: literally 'pray God'. A kneeling desk for private prayer.
quote: with a _prie-Dieu_, all its furniture

text: France was overwhelmingly Catholic, but the Charter of 1830 guaranteed freedom of worship; a Protestant could not be harassed for his creed.
quote: liberty of conscience is established in France

text: The Order of Christ, the highest order of chivalry awarded by the pope.
quote: has made him a knight of Jesus Christ

term: Homer carrying his guide … Belisarius begging
text: Popular sentimental engravings: the blind poet Homer, and the Byzantine general Belisarius, said by legend to have been blinded and reduced to begging.
quote: Homer carrying his guide

text: Kerseymere is a fine twilled wool; nankeen a sturdy yellowish cotton, originally from Nanjing. A coat 'in the fashion of 1811' was nearly thirty years out of date.
quote: a white kerseymere waistcoat, and nankeen pantaloons

text: Old ships stripped of masts and used as floating prisons. Britain packed French prisoners of war into them during the Napoleonic Wars.
quote: consigned to the hulks, whence he had escaped

text: The Greeks rose against Ottoman rule in 1821. At Navarino (1827) British, French and Russian fleets destroyed the Turkish-Egyptian fleet, and in 1832 the Bavarian prince Otto became the first King of Greece.
quote: After the battle of Navarino, when the Greek government

text: Spa towns in the Pyrenees famous for their mineral springs. Badhaus is German for 'bath-house'.
quote: equal to those at Bagnères, Luchon, and Cauterets

text: Augustin Grisier, the most celebrated fencing master in Paris, and Dumas's own teacher.
quote: every other day Grisier comes to my house

text: The galop was a lively, fast ballroom dance in quick time; both it and the waltz were the fashionable dances of the 1830s.
quote: the whirl of the waltz and galop

text: The forget-me-not. In the language of flowers it means faithful remembrance.
quote: the other with one of myosotis

text: Slang, borrowed from English, for a fashionable celebrity everyone wants to see.
quote: we shall have this ‘lion’

text: Fanny Elssler, the Austrian star ballerina, created a sensation at the Paris Opéra dancing the cachucha, a Spanish dance, in the ballet Le Diable boiteux (1836).
quote: Elssler was dancing in _Le Diable

text: The Institut de France, which unites the national academies. The French Academy judges language and literature; the Academy of Sciences, science. Albert mocks a scientist admitted to the former for his prose style.
quote: he immediately laid his discovery before the Institute

text: Grades of the Legion of Honour, France's chief decoration, rising from knight (chevalier) to officer, commander and higher.
quote: was only a knight of the Legion

text: The July Monarchy of Louis-Philippe, set up after the 1830 revolution. Voting and power went with wealth, which is why a millionaire's title seems 'the finest' to Danglars.
quote: the finest title under the royalty of July

term: their signature is worth five per cent
text: When a bank failed, creditors recovered only a fraction of what was owed. The count means Franck & Poulmann's paper will now fetch five centimes on the franc.
quote: their signature is worth five per cent

text: 'Setting out for Syria', a song written by Napoleon's stepdaughter Hortense that became the unofficial Bonapartist anthem.
quote: had sung _Partant pour la Syrie_

text: Across the Arab world and the East, eating bread and salt together under someone's roof creates a sacred bond: host and guest become friends, and may not thereafter act as enemies.
quote: eaten bread and salt under the same roof

text: Sweet, perfumed dessert grapes, grown here in a heated hothouse to ripen in a northern July.
quote: gathered a bunch of Muscatel grapes

text: Long journeys were made in stages between post-houses where horses were changed; 'the first stage' is the first post-house out of Marseilles.
quote: took place on the first stage

text: From Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 1: crimes will come to light however deeply buried.
quote: Foul deeds will rise

text: The writing on the wall in the Book of Daniel: a hand appears at King Belshazzar's feast and writes words foretelling his doom.
quote: _mene, mene, tekel upharsin_

text: The rider on one of the lead horses of a post-carriage, who drove in place of a coachman.
quote: I stopped the postilion

text: A lead-lined coffin was sealed so that a body could be carried a long way, here from Provence to the family vault in Paris.
quote: I had him put into a leaden coffin

text: Royalists' name for Napoleon. The marquise means General d'Épinay was killed just before Napoleon's return from Elba in 1815.
quote: some days before the usurper returned

text: A drink of orange juice and sweetened water, often given to invalids as a cooling drink.
quote: a bottle of orangeade, her usual beverage

text: Of common, non-noble birth. To a proud old aristocrat, a merchant's son, however honourable, was no match for a noble heiress.
quote: Morrel was of plebeian extraction

text: In the Don Juan legend (and Mozart's Don Giovanni), the statue of a murdered Commander walks with heavy stone steps to drag the seducer to hell.
quote: the footsteps of the commander did Don Juan

text: Before the civil wedding, both families signed a marriage contract fixing dowry and property before a notary and witnesses. In practice it was the binding public betrothal.
quote: a comedy called the signature of the contract

text: Two brooding Romantic heroes: Byron's Manfred (1817), tormented by guilt, and Antony, hero of Dumas's own sensational play Antony (1831).
quote: I imitate neither Manfred nor Anthony

text: Tetanus, or lockjaw, causes violent spasms and rigid limbs. The doctor notes that poisoning by certain plant alkaloids looks almost exactly the same.
quote: I discovered symptoms of tetanus

text: A grain was an apothecary's weight of about 65 milligrams, so six grains is under half a gram.
quote: there were six grains

text: Latin: 'to err is human'.
quote: this axiom, _errare humanum est_

text: A formal judicial inquiry into a suspicious death, with a post-mortem. For a crown prosecutor, one in his own house would mean public scandal.
quote: an inquest will become necessary

text: Correggio, the Italian Renaissance painter, was famous for his Penitent Magdalen: Mary Magdalene in tearful, beautiful grief.
quote: a head like that of a Magdalen by Correggio

text: Paris's great cemetery, opened in 1804 on a hillside east of the city, crowded with the family vaults of the wealthy.
quote: the cemetery of Père-Lachaise

text: Black carriages hired for a funeral to carry mourners behind the hearse.
quote: a long file of mourning-coaches

text: Latin, from Horace's Odes: 'a man steadfast of purpose', whom nothing can shake.
quote: _Tenacem propositi virum_

text: A member of the revolutionary National Convention of 1793, which voted the king's death. Marengo (1800) and Austerlitz (1805) were two of Napoleon's greatest victories.
quote: the old Conventionalist of ’93

text: Latin: 'I am going to the country'. Beauchamp calls death a retreat to a country cottage.
quote: ‘_Eo rus_, and all will be over.’

text: Etiquette laid down fixed periods of mourning for each degree of kinship; during them a family withdrew from society and avoided celebrations such as weddings.
quote: during the prescribed three months

term: a much more nervous than sanguine temperament
text: Old medical theory sorted people into temperaments: the 'sanguine' (ruddy, full-blooded) were thought prone to apoplexy, the 'nervous' (slight, excitable) were not.
quote: a much more nervous than sanguine temperament

term: you know they are my witnesses
text: A marriage contract and wedding required witnesses, usually close friends of each party.
quote: you know they are my witnesses

text: A writing desk with a drop-front writing surface and many small drawers, often including a hidden compartment.
quote: an old secretaire which had been neglected

text: At that date Napoleon was still on Elba and Louis XVIII had reigned for less than a year. Bonapartist clubs met in secret, waiting for the emperor's return.
quote: held February 5th, 1815

text: A member of the Council of State, a senior body of government officials: not a man you would expect to find on a coachman's box.
quote: we shall be driven by a State-Councillor

text: 'Field-marshal' here translates maréchal de camp, a general's rank equal to major-general, not the much higher marshal of France.
quote: he has made me a baron and a field-marshal

text: A quay on the Right Bank of the Seine near the Hôtel de Ville, where steps led down to the river.
quote: at that part of the Quai des Ormes

text: The language of the duel: an insulted gentleman demanded 'satisfaction' with weapons. Seconds (witnesses) checked the weapons and rules, and could be called on to attest the fight was fair.
quote: without demanding honorable reparation

text: Bagni di Lucca, a spa town in the Tuscan hills whose casino was one of the first licensed gambling houses in Europe.
quote: at the gaming-table of the baths of Lucca

text: Seravezza, near Carrara, is famous for its marble quarries; Michelangelo took stone from there.
quote: buried in the quarries of Saravezza

text: Minerva, goddess of wisdom, carried an impenetrable shield; Sappho was the ancient Greek poet of love. Eugénie is armoured against Andrea's sighs.
quote: they might have been said to fall on the shield of Minerva

text: French: 'living pictures', a fashionable entertainment in which costumed people posed motionless to recreate a painting.
quote: one of the _tableaux vivants_

text: A tale by E. T. A. Hoffmann: Antonia has a glorious voice, but a weakness of the chest means that singing will kill her.
quote: like Antonia in the _Cremona

text: Sigismond Thalberg, a virtuoso pianist of the 1830s and Liszt's great rival in Paris.
quote: she plays the piano like Thalberg

text: A cavatina is a short, simple operatic song. In Italian 'bravo' praises a man, 'brava' a woman, 'bravi' a group: Danglars shows off by using all three.
quote: do you hear that delightful cavatina?

text: In Hamlet Act 1, King Claudius tells the grieving prince that losing fathers is the common lot of nature, so mourning should not go on too long.
quote: as Claudius said to Hamlet

term: leave the spoons in their cups
text: English tea-table etiquette of the time: leaving the spoon in the cup signalled that you wanted no more tea.
quote: in the English fashion, to leave the spoons
